Set 1.text: A shop marks a laptop 25% above its cost price and then offers a 12% discount on the marked price. What is the shop's profit percentage?
Set 1.working: 1.25 × 0.88 = 1.10, so the selling price is 110% of cost: a 10% profit.

options: All people who analyse information are researchers.
Set 1.working: The students who are researchers must analyse information, so at least some students do. Nothing is known about the rest.

Set 1.text: A college says: "Students who joined our internship programme had higher placement rates than other students, so the programme improves employability." Which statement, if true, most weakens this conclusion?
options: Students with higher grades were more likely to be selected for the programme.
The programme runs for eight weeks.
Placement rates rose at most colleges this year.
A few students did not finish the programme.
Set 1.working: If stronger students were chosen for the programme, they might have been placed anyway, so the programme may not be the cause. A general rise affects both groups equally.

Set 1.text: Five students - P, Q, R, S and T - are ranked 1st to 5th with no ties. P ranks higher than Q. R ranks lower than S but higher than T. Q ranks higher than T. Which student must be ranked 5th?
Set 1.working: T is below R (and so below S) and below Q (and so below P). T is below all four others, so T must be 5th.

Set 1.text: Every student selected for Research is also selected for Entrepreneurship. Every student selected for Entrepreneurship is also selected for Leadership. A student is NOT selected for Leadership. Which statement must be true?
options: The student may still be selected for Entrepreneurship.
The student is selected for Research.
The student is selected for neither Research nor Entrepreneurship.
The student must be selected for some other activity.
Set 1.working: Research ⊂ Entrepreneurship ⊂ Leadership. Outside Leadership means outside both smaller groups too.

Set 1.text: Four presentations - W, X, Y and Z - are scheduled Monday to Thursday, one per day. W is before X. Y is the day immediately after Z. Z is on Monday or Tuesday. X is not on Wednesday. Which presentation must be on Thursday?
Set 1.working: If Z is Monday, Y is Tuesday and W, X take Wednesday and Thursday with W first, so X is Thursday. If Z is Tuesday, Y is Wednesday and W, X take Monday and Thursday, so X is again Thursday.

Set 1.text: A university grouped students by the number of practical sessions they attended and compared their average project scores (chart below). Which statement is best supported by the chart?
options: Scores rise with sessions up to about 9-11 sessions, then level off.
Attending practical sessions causes higher project scores.

Set 1.working: Averages climb from 58 to 73 and then stay about the same (72). The chart shows an association, not proof of cause, and the gains are not equal per session.

Set 1.text: A project has three tasks. Task X takes 3 hours, Task Y takes 2 hours and Task Z takes 4 hours. Z can start only after X is finished; Y has no dependency. With two people working in parallel, what is the minimum time to finish all three tasks?
Set 1.working: X then Z must run one after the other (3 + 4 = 7 hours), while the second person does Y alongside. The chain X→Z sets the minimum: 7 hours.

Set 1.text: You must order equipment with a total budget of ₹50,000 (including delivery), and it must arrive within 10 days. Which supplier meets both conditions?
options: Supplier P: ₹44,000 + ₹4,000 delivery, arrives in 12 days
Supplier Q: ₹46,500 + ₹2,500 delivery, arrives in 9 days
Supplier R: ₹47,000 + ₹3,500 delivery, arrives in 6 days
Supplier S: ₹49,000 with free delivery, arrives in 11 days
Set 1.working: P and S are too late. R costs ₹50,500, over budget. Q costs ₹49,000 and arrives in 9 days.

Compare it with the existing method
Continue with the old method until required to change

Set 1.text: You are most likely to adopt a new technology when:
options: It becomes widely accepted in your field

Set 1.text: Which ability do you think will become increasingly important across many careers?

options: Develop new skills within the same field
Combine your existing expertise with a new field
Wait until the direction of the industry becomes clearer

options: Learn it if it could create future opportunities
Learn it only when there is a clear application
Prioritise skills directly relevant to my current path

Short-term exposure through workshops or events

options: Build something I can demonstrate professionally

options: Know exactly which skills I need to strengthen
Have a general sense but not a clear picture

options: Learn enough to solve the immediate problem
Find someone who can teach you
Look for an alternative way around the problem

options: Identify adjacent career options using your existing skills
Wait to see whether the situation improves

options: Quickly interact and learn from people
Establish a routine as soon as possible
Experiment until you find what works

options: A highly specialised technical or professional sector
A people-focused service or social sector
A commercial, entrepreneurial or competitive sector

options: Build deep expertise in one industry
Choose the industry with the strongest growth opportunities
Choose the industry that best matches your interests and values

options: Relocate if the opportunity significantly supports my career

Set 1.text: When you imagine your career 10 years from now, which statement best describes your preference?
options: I want to become a recognised expert in one area
I want to grow into leadership and greater responsibility
I want to build a career that allows multiple transitions
I want to develop a combination of expertise across different areas

Set 1.text: Which statement best describes your approach to your long-term career?
options: I prefer to define a clear destination and work systematically toward it
I prefer a direction but want flexibility to change along the way
I prefer to explore opportunities and let experience shape my direction
I want to continuously reinvent my career as my interests and the world change

Why did you originally choose this degree? Select up to TWO.
options: Advice from family, teachers or mentors.
Entrance score, eligibility or availability influenced the choice.
I was uncertain and selected from the options available.

options: Choosing a field that does not suit me.

Affording further education or a career transition.
